reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator actively promotes purchasing a StrongBlock node as a passive-income investment, claiming that viewers can recover the 10-STRONG cost in about 100 days and earn substantial monthly rewards. It directs viewers toward creating a node through MetaMask, paying ETH gas and a recurring fee, and reinvesting or withdrawing the rewards, while the creator states that he purchased a node and offers assistance. The disclaimers and risk acknowledgment do not remove the concrete solicitation and unusually strong return framing.

citations.quote: creating a blockchain node and earning rewards. So this is one thing I love, is earning a passive income.

it costs 10 strong quite tokens alright and you create the node and it's hosted for you in Singapore, obviously the date it's created and the estimated rewards is point one of a Strong Token per day, so in essence roughly within 100 days you should get your 10 strong back between 100 and 109 days
if you want any assistance in creating your own blockchain node which is really simple just drop me a line not a problem
what you'll need is a Metamask wallet, you'll also need to pay a monthly fee of $14.95 and you can do that with ETH from your MetaMask wallet
Please have extra ETH for GAS FEES.

opening.argument: The speaker presents a conditional investment discussion, not a promise of certain profit. He tells viewers to do their own research, explicitly calls the opportunity risky, and conditions his repayment example on the token price staying the same. Those qualifications matter: a calculation based on a changing market price is not a guaranteed payout. The better reading is investment commentary that leaves the decision and its risks with the viewer.

citations.quote: not financial advice by the way, do your own research
it's risky by the way
if the price stays the same then you know happy that is you've paid for your investment

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument identifies a strong repayment estimate, but its characterization underplays the speaker's qualifications. He calls the investment risky, identifies a recurring fee, and makes the repayment illustration conditional on the token price. Those details do not prove the estimate correct; they do challenge the claim that viewers are being offered an unconditional return.

citations.quote: it's risky by the way
you'll also need to pay a monthly fee of $14.95
if the price stays the same then you know happy that is you've paid for your investment

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cautions do not erase the central pitch. The speaker tells viewers they should recover the 10-token cost in roughly 100 days, then translates projected rewards into substantial monthly income. A condition about token price does not establish that the reward rate will persist or that the initial cost can actually be recovered.

citations.quote: so in essence roughly within 100 days you should get your 10 strong back between 100 and 109 days
looking at 1,573 pounds per month in rewards so you can see how powerful this particular project can be

opening.argument: The video is structured as a walkthrough of a hosted-node system. The speaker introduces it as an overview, explains the wallet and fee requirements, moves to a market-data site, and shows his own node and recorded rewards. Explaining the interface and costs is useful operational information even when the subject involves an investment. His personal demonstration does not, by itself, establish that he is guaranteeing the same result to viewers.

So let's pop on to coinmarketcap.com.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument treats the setup instructions and offer to answer questions as solicitation. Those details also fit a walkthrough: viewers need to know the wallet, fees, and steps to understand the system being discussed. Showing a node with recorded rewards is a demonstration of what the interface displays, not proof that the speaker promised every viewer a completed payout.

citations.quote: what you'll need is a Metamask wallet, you'll also need to pay a monthly fee of $14.95
Rewards 0.36 I've had it for three four days now

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is built around the claimed financial payoff, not merely how the software operates. The speaker gives an estimated time to recover the purchase cost, describes reinvesting rewards into another node, and offers to help viewers create one. Displaying a node account does not verify that viewers can realize the projected returns.

citations.quote: roughly within 100 days you should get your 10 strong back between 100 and 109 days
you can obviously reinvest that and buy another node
if you want any assistance in creating your own blockchain node which is really simple just drop me a line not a problem

opening.argument: What is shown can be understood as a paid hosted-node service: the speaker identifies the token cost, hosting arrangement, monthly charge, and gas fees. The supplied material does not show a request to send funds to the speaker, disclose wallet credentials, or recruit a downline. Those absent mechanisms do not prove the service is sound, but they matter before treating a discussion of its price and possible rewards as evidence of a deceptive scheme.

citations.quote: it costs 10 strong quite tokens alright and you create the node and it's hosted for you in Singapore
you'll also need to pay a monthly fee of $14.95 and you can do that with ETH from your MetaMask wallet
Please have extra ETH for GAS FEES.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument points to real costs, but a token purchase, service fee, and gas fee are not, on their own, proof of fraud. The speaker discloses those costs and describes withdrawal as an alternative to reinvestment. The record does not establish that payment goes to him or that viewers must recruit anyone to receive the discussed rewards.

citations.quote: you'll also need to pay a monthly fee of $14.95 and you can do that with ETH from your MetaMask wallet
you can obviously reinvest that and buy another node or you can withdraw it
Please have extra ETH for GAS FEES.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A personal payment request or downline is not necessary for the concern at issue. The speaker promotes paying for a node on the expectation of recurring token rewards, gives an approximate period for recovering its cost, and presents reinvestment as an option. Disclosing fees does not substantiate the projected returns.
